subject: Quantico pilot: pacing + GPU tiling estimates for dedicated footprint
messages:
From: Eric Sun <eric@quantico.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Delgado <procurement@quantico.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing ask — preliminary usage sample attached

Hi Priyom / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a 6-week pilot (internal engineers + 3 production endpoints) and need a quick sizing recommendation for a dedicated footprint so we can budget and route procurement.

Quick summary of our expected profile (see attached sample for per-endpoint traces):
- Expected steady-state: ~15 rps across endpoints (combined), average request ~120 tokens (prompt+response).
- Peak bursts: short spikes up to ~200 rps for 30–90s (marketing pushes).
- 40% of calls need 1k+ context (historical chat), rest are ~256–512 ctx.
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 250ms for end-to-end generation (we can accept slightly higher for the long-context calls).
- We’d like a plan that keeps production available during bursts and leaves room for warm-up.

Can you provide: 1) a tokens/sec peak estimate, 2) ballpark GPU count and type for Dedicated, and 3) suggested headroom percentage for safe commit?

Attached: quantico-usage-sample.csv (session traces). Procurement contact Sofia is cc’d for pricing timelines.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

—Eric
Principal ML Eng, Quantico AI
[Attachment: quantico-usage-sample.csv (CSV, 54KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Sun <eric@quantico.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Sofia Delgado <procurement@quantico.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — preliminary usage sample attached

Thanks Eric — this is helpful. Quick clarifying Qs before I lock numbers:
- Which model family do you want to serve (open-7B, 13B, or a fine-tuned 7B)? Different families shift tokens/sec by ~2–3x.
- Is prefix/KV caching acceptable for the 40% long-context flows? That substantially reduces load if sessions are repeated.
- Any hard requirement on P99? You mentioned p95 <= 250ms — want us to target p95 <= 200ms for the pilot or stick to 250ms?

Initial back-of-envelope (assume: fine-tuned 7B, quantized q4_0, Redwood runtime optimizations, mixed precision, A10G class hardware):
- Peak tokens/sec calculation: peak_rps * avg_tokens approximates token ingress. Using your peak 200 rps and average 120 tokens -> 24,000 tokens/sec.
- Adjusting for long context: 40% of 200 rps are ~80 calls at 1024 tokens -> adds incremental token work. Recompute: 
  - Short calls (120 tokens): 120 calls * 120 = 14,400 tokens/sec
  - Long calls (1024 tokens): 80 calls * 1024 = 81,920 tokens/sec (but note: we can reuse KV/prefix for many long calls — if not reused, worst-case tokens/sec shoots up)
  - So worst-case uncached peak tokens/sec ≈ 96,320 tokens/sec.
- Practical throttling assumption: we design for *no-worst-case* but for a realistic worst-burst with 50% cache hit on the long calls -> effective peak tokens/sec ≈ 58,160 tokens/sec.

Per-GPU throughput estimate (our runtime on A10G, fine-tuned 7B, mixed batching): ~7,000–8,000 effective tokens/sec under production batching for mixed 256/512 loads. For long 1024-context calls throughput per GPU drops ~1.8x for that batch mix.

Sizing math (conservative):
- Use 7,000 tokens/sec per A10G equivalent.
- Required GPUs = ceil(58,160 / 7,000) = 9 GPUs.
- Add headroom: we recommend 35% buffer for autoscale, warm-up, and model variance -> 9 * 1.35 ≈ 12 GPUs reserved.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: start with 4 GPUs as a canary (route 25% of traffic), validate your real cache-hit rates and p95s, then ramp to 8, and hold 12 as reserved burst capacity.
- Autoscale: allow burst to 16 GPUs for very short pushes (reduces user-visible queuing).
- Cost tradeoff: if you can strict-cach long-history sessions (session affinity + KV cache), you can drop reserve to ~8 GPUs.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm model variant and whether KV/prefix caching is acceptable.
2) If ok, Ben can draft a Dedicated proposal with a 12-GPU reserved slab and burst to 16.
3) We'll schedule a short p95 validation run during the canary.

I’ll follow up with a succinct internal note for pricing + ops (cc’ing Ben & Marissa).

—Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Key commercial asks to consider:

- Discount tiers: recommend a 15% pilot discount and a 12-month reserved commit at standard enterprise rates if they commit within 60 days.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for dedicated slab; latency SLOs governed by per-route p95 checks (we can include a remediation credit schedule).

Eric / Sofia: attachment is a draft — high level pricing + timelines. Priyom, can you validate the 12GPU reserved orientation still looks correct if they confirm KV caching? If caching reduces reserve to 8, we’ll note that as an alternate.

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — final ops recommendation and action items

Internal summary (copying externally for transparency):

Final recommended configuration (pilot-ready):
- Reserved slab: 12 A10G-equivalent GPUs (baseline).
- Burst/autoscale: allow up to 16 GPUs for short bursts; scale-down cool-off 10m.
- Canary rollout: 4 GPUs (canary) -> validate p95 and cache hit -> ramp to 8 -> promote to 12 reserved.

Throughput & latency expectations (measured under Redwood runtime, mixed batching):
- Effective tokens/sec per A10G (mixed load): ~7,000 tps.
- Expected effective peak tokens/sec with 50% cache on long calls: ~58k tps -> 9 GPUs nominal -> 12 GPUs with 35% headroom.
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for typical 256–512 calls on 12 GPUs. Long-context (1024+) will be 200–350ms depending on cache hit; if they enable prefix caching we expect long-context p95 to fall below 250ms.

Operational mitigations to hit SLOs:
- Enable KV/prefix caching for conversation threads where possible.
- Configure continuous batching with a 20ms batching window to improve per-GPU throughput without materially changing p95 for short calls.
- Reserve a small enqueue buffer and priority lanes for low-latency routes (e.g., customer-facing endpoints).

Action items:
- Ben: finalize the draft proposal with 12-GPU baseline and optional 8-GPU cached plan; include pricing for burst to 16. (Due: EOD Thu 8/13)
- Marissa: confirm SLA language and conversion terms we want for the pilot-to-commit clause. (Due: Fri 8/14)
- Priyom: prepare a 30-min validation checklist and runbook for the canary (p95 test vectors, cache validation, failure/fallback). I’ll schedule the run with Quantico once proposal is signed.

Eric / Sofia — happy to proceed when you confirm model variant + whether you can enable KV caching. If you prefer a different GPU class (A100/H100) we can re-run the math — but A10G gives the best cost/throughput balance for a fine-tuned 7B here.

Thanks everyone —
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
